description: Route Model policy and target-specific calibration used to rank all-SIMD, all-SIMT, and mixed SIMD/SIMT candidates. Model-neutral hardware measurements are referenced from microbenchmark_profile instead of duplicated here.

policy.description: Admission policy for turning a ranking into an actionable route decision. Only minimum_confidence_for_decision is currently consumed by the C++ loader.
policy.notes: Analytical payloads use SYS_CNT cycles, but Event-calibrated structural residuals make final values selection scores rather than literal measured cycles. Low-confidence rankings may act only inside the bounded calibration domain and must still pass target, unsupported-term, legality, and gain gates.

selection_calibration.description: Route-specific calibration that converts analytical resource costs into relative selection scores and bounds where those scores may make decisions. Mixed cost is partitioned from the materializable anchor plan; the removed legacy mixed_simd_fraction blend no longer participates.
selection_calibration.source: Bounded development activation fitted to repeated Ascend950PR Event runs for masked-rowwise, tiny-gather-dot, and triangular-solve sample domains. In v10, all-SIMD raw cost became A_SIMD * (1 + Pstruct); domain all_simd multipliers preserve the v9 Event-anchored score scale without an online dependency on A_SIMT. Mixed scoring uses the exact materializable anchor resource partition. Setup proxies were reclassified on 2026-07-30; no directional SIMD/SIMT boundary latency has been measured.

coverage.description: Feature-domain limits within which Event-calibrated structural ranking is admitted; these are model validity bounds rather than hardware limits. The masked-rowwise tensor bound includes the measured FBGEMM scope_b8 workload whose current TTIR analysis reports max_tensor_numel=128. Larger rowwise programs remain out of domain until dedicated calibration exists.

simd_structural_penalty_ratio.description: Additive SIMD-only residual ratios for irregular addressing, mask materialization, reductions, loops, control flow, tiny dot, and rank-1 indirect reduction patterns. Their sum multiplies A_SIMD; A_SIMT never participates in the all-SIMD cost.

event_route_score_multiplier.description: Low-confidence route-relative residual calibration. For each bounded feature domain, calibrated_score = raw_analytical_structural_score * route_multiplier. The v10 all_simd multiplier migrates the independently computed A_SIMD * (1 + Pstruct) raw score onto the existing Event-anchored domain scale; the other route multipliers retain the measured median NPU Event ratios on A5 card 0. Raw scores and multipliers are both emitted in the report. all_simt_only_validated may promote only a BackendConditional pure-SIMT route whose whole-kernel correctness was independently verified.

masked_rowwise_reduction.source: A5 card 0, FBGEMM T128/D128/H8/num_warps4, 30 warmup + 100 NPU Event samples: median all-SIMD 68.9340 us, all-SIMT 26.7795 us, Auto mixed 36.0365 us; all routes correctness PASS.

tiny_irregular_dot.source: A5 card 0, gather-dot-min M16/N16/K16/num_warps4, one process with routes interleaved after 50 warmup, 200 NPU Event samples each: median all-SIMD 29.2525 us and correctness PASS; all-SIMT 25.1570 us but mismatched 256/256 elements; C++-materialized 2-scope mixed 25.3980 us and correctness PASS after lowering buffer-semantics identity vtranspose to copy and using cross-core GSS instead of the delayed variant whose split-side anchor interval is reversed. Mixed is 13.18% faster than all-SIMD.

triangular_solve_loop.source: A5 card 0, solve-tril BT16/num_warps4, one process with routes interleaved after 50 warmup, 200 NPU Event samples each: median all-SIMD 22.1160 us, all-SIMT 21.9315 us, C++-materialized mixed 22.3130 us; all routes correctness PASS. The all-SIMT advantage is below the 10% production switch margin, so Post Check keeps the all-SIMD baseline.

attention_indirect_gqa.source: A5 card 0, ROPE GQA fwd T16/R16/N16/num_warps4/BS=1, compile_mode routes measured separately: median SIMD 241 us, SIMT-only 50 us, C++-materialized mixed 17 us; all routes correctness PASS. Mixed is 14.2x faster than SIMD. Multipliers derived from latency ratios: m_simd=119.1, m_simt=0.211, m_mixed=1.0.

indirect_elementwise.source: A5 card 0, causal_conv1d_fwd T256/D16/num_warps4, compile_mode routes measured separately: median SIMD 4.5 us, SIMT-only 4.7 us, C++-materialized mixed 4.4 us; all routes correctness PASS. Mixed advantage is below the 10% production switch margin, so Post Check keeps the all-SIMD baseline. Multipliers derived from latency ratios: m_simd=67.65, m_simt=0.123, m_mixed=1.0.

dynamic_loop_elementwise.source: A5 card 0, silu_mul_static_tensorwise_quant for cutlass_moe T256/num_warps4, compile_mode routes measured separately: median SIMD 16.3 us, SIMT-only 3.9 us, legacy simd_simt 3.7 us. Kernel has no SIMT anchor (mixed inapplicable), whole-kernel pure SIMT is native. SIMT-only is 4.2x faster than SIMD. Multipliers derived from latency ratios anchored on all_simt_only: m_simd=67.52, m_simt=1.0, m_mixed=1.0.

i32.bitop.description: Integer bitwise ops (and/or/xor/shl/shr). Microbenchmark (bitops_simd_microbench, 16M elements) shows no scalarization: throughput equals f32.add, so the 96x placeholder was wrong. cycles/element 0.00414 vs add 0.00488.

i32.min.description: Integer min. Microbenchmark throughput matches f32.add (factor ~0.88 measured); rounded to 1.0.

i32.rem.description: Integer remainder. Microbenchmark: ~1.47x f32.add cost (memory-bandwidth-contaminated upper bound), replacing the 12x placeholder.

convert.bitcast.description: Tensor bitcast. Microbenchmark confirms free register reinterpretation (factor ~0.92).

memory.description: Model-specific all-SIMD memory fallback rates. vector_mte2 and mte3 plus confidence are consumed; hbm is retained only as documentary legacy context.
memory.source: Selection-model seed retained for v4 score continuity; 202.25 B/SYS_CNT-cycle corresponds to 200 GB/s and must not be presented as the davidV100 75/71 GB/s data-mover specification
memory.note: Model-specific fallback, not shared microbenchmark evidence

camodel_effective.description: Workload-effective CaModel issue rates retained as fallback calibration context. The current Route Model consumes only the predicate rate from the nested rate map.
camodel_effective.note: These are effective issue rates for one FBGEMM workload, including its dependencies and stalls. They are fallback calibration seeds, not isolated instruction peak throughput or latency.

shuffle.description: SIMT workload-effective shuffle rate resolved from the shared runtime-loop microbenchmark. Route-level generalization confidence is intentionally lower than measurement repeatability.

memory.description: SIMT workload-effective GM load/store rates resolved from sequential rotating runtime-loop measurements. Indirect/random/coalescing behavior is not calibrated by these rates.

mixed_setup_fallback.note: These values are mode1(empty SIMT plus tail barrier) minus mode6(barrier only) in a branch-heavy harness. They contain no SIMD phase and are used only as conservative setup fallbacks. Directional SIMD-to-SIMT, SIMT-to-SIMD, and dependent UB hand-off costs remain unmeasured.

scan.description: Single-block cumsum microbenchmark on A5; latency is nearly flat for n>=1024.
